Bug_Title: NP: Null value is guaranteed to be dereferenced (NP_GUARANTEED_DEREF)
Bug_Details:
There is a statement or branch that if executed guarantees that
      a value is null at this point, and that
      value that is guaranteed to be dereferenced
      (except on forward paths involving runtime exceptions).
       Note that a check such as
    if (x == null) throw new NullPointerException();
    is treated as a dereference of x. if (x == null) throw new NullPointerException(); x
Bug_Explanation: The bug is demonstrated by calling a method on a null object that will throw a NullPointerException at runtime. This is because the nullString object is null, and calling a method on it will result in a NullPointerException.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method of the NullPointerBugExample class instance. This method tries to call the toUpperCase method on a null object, which will result in a NullPointerException.
